newsitem.title: USA: Washington congresswoman wins House leadership race.
newsitem.headline: Washington congresswoman wins House leadership race.

text.p: In a vote seen as a victory for Speaker Newt Gingrich, Washington Republican Representative Jennifer Dunn easily won a House party post Wednesday, heading off a conservative who complained about drift among current leaders.

By a 129-85 Dunn was elected vice chairman of the House Republican Conference, replacing New York Representative Susan Molinari, who is leaving Congress to become a weekend news anchor for CBS television.

Dunn beat Iowa Republican Representative Jim Nussle, who had the backing of restive conservatives. Nussle publicly complained that House Republican leaders were doing a poor job formulating and communicating the party's agenda.

House Republicans took a pounding earlier this year when they held up a disaster relief bill in an effort to force President Clinton to accept non-related provisions. Public opinion polls also show voters believe a tax cut legislation written by Republicans would primarily favour the rich.
Dunn, already Republican Conference secretary, was perceived as allied with the current leadership. She ran partly on a platform of greater visibility for women in the Republican party.
The election makes Dunn the highest ranking Republican woman in the House.
"Today's election was not about sending a message, but about who can be the best messenger," Dunn said.
"If you believe hard work should be rewarded and if you believe in opportunity for women and that substance counts, you belong in the Republican party," she said.
